title: Multiple split-system air conditioners and air-to-air heat pumps (VRF air conditioners) - Specification
scope: 1.1 This standard covers the requirements, method of test and the standard condition for determining the capacity and efficiency ratings of air-cooled air conditioners and air-to-air heat pumps with rated voltage up to and including 250 V, 50 Hz a.c. for single phase and up to and including 415 V, 50 Hz a.c. for three phase power supply. NOTE - The air conditioners covered under the scope of this standard are commonly known as variable refrigerant flow (VRF) air conditioners. 1.2 This standard is applicable to the following equipments: a) Basic multi-split systems; b) Modular multi-split systems; and c) Modular heat recovery multi-split systems. These multi-split systems include air-to-air systems with non-ducted and/or ducted indoor units with integral fans and indoor units supplied without fans. 1.3 This standard is limited to the following: a) Residential, commercial, and industrial split-system air conditioners and heat pumps; b) Factory-made, electrically driven, and use mechanical compression; c) Single and multiple-circuit splitsystems which utilize one or more compressors with no more than two steps of control of the outdoor unit; or d) Split-systems with a single refrigeration circuit which utilize one or more variable-speed compressors or alternative compressor combinations for varying the capacity of the system by three or more steps. The split-systems are designed to operate with a combination of one or more outdoor units and two or more indoor units designed for individual operation, and such modular systems are capable of transferring recovered heat from one or more indoor units to other units in the same system. The requirements of testing and rating covered in this standard are based on the use of matched assemblies. 1.4 This standard is not applicable to the rating and testing of the following: a) Water-cooled or water source equipment; b) Mobile (single-duct) units having a condenser exhaust duct; c) Individual assemblies not constituting a complete refrigeration system; d) Equipment using the absorption refrigeration cycle; e) Unitary and split air conditioners covered under IS 1391 (Part 1) and (Part 2); f) Ducted and packaged air conditioners covered under IS 8148; and g) Evaporative air cooler covered under IS 3315. For the purpose of testing in India, standard test conditions T1 for cooling and H1 for heating shall be followed as defined in this standard.

title: LAB INSTRUMENTS FOR CBM EVALUATION - CODE OF PRACTICE PART 1 MUD BALANCE
scope: Mud balance is a very essential and versatile instrument for quick and accurate measurement of density and specific gravity of the cement slurries, drilling fluids or any type of liquid/slurry in oil and gas field operations like drilling, cementing, hydrofracturing as well as in laboratory experiment/design purpose. Mud balance consists of a graduated beam with bubble level as an indicator and a weight slider along with the length in one side. The other side contains with sample cup of fixed volume with a lid cover. The lid of sample cup is having with a hole at the centre to escape the extra fluid in cup. A sliderweight can be moved along the beam, and a bubble indicates when the beam is level. Density is read at the point where the slider-weight sits on the beam at level.

title: LAB INSTRUMENTS FOR CBM EVALUATION - CODE OF PRACTICE PART 3 TURBIDITY METER
scope: This standard covers the turbidity meter which is a very essential and useful instrument in oil field as well as in CBM operation for characterization and quality control of injection water, waste water, effluent water, chemicals etc for measurement of turbidity. Turbidity is an optical property of the water and it indicates the haziness or opaqueness of water. The turbidity is caused by the suspended particle and coloured material in water. In CBM, turbidity of water is measured by nephelometry (90 degree scattering with respect to the centre line of the incident light path) and turbidity is measured in NTU unit (nephelometric turbidity units). The higher intensity of scattered light, higher will be turbidity. However, the turbidity of water depends upon the size, shape and composition of the suspended particle and wavelength of the incident light also.
